issues.description: Field Farm.animals: The UML in the problem statement (Farm class) declares the field as List<Animal>, while the textual instructions later (Part 3) state that the aggregation must be realized using a Set implemented as a HashSet. This conflicting specification (List vs Set) in the problem statement makes it unclear which collection type students should implement and whether uniqueness semantics are required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: update the UML diagram to show animals: Set<Animal> (to match the textual requirement about HashSet and uniqueness), and/or add a clarifying sentence in the problem statement that the UML should be interpreted as Set<Animal>. Prefer changing the UML to animals: Set<Animal> and explicitly note HashSet in the class description so students clearly implement a HashSet for uniqueness.

issues.description: Field Farm.animals in the solution: The solution implementation declares private List<Animal> animals and initializes it with new ArrayList<>(), but the problem statement explicitly requires the aggregation to be a Set implemented as a HashSet to enforce unique animals. The solution's choice of List conflicts with the textual requirement and may mislead students about the expected data structure and uniqueness behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by changing the Farm.animals field to be of type Set<Animal> (java.util.Set) and initialize it as new HashSet<>() in the no-argument constructor; update the getter/setter signatures accordingly and adjust addAnimal to call animals.add(animal). If List semantics were intended instead, update the problem statement to remove the HashSet/Set requirement. Prefer modifying the solution to use Set to preserve the stated uniqueness requirement.
